title: A computational framework for predictive modeling of refugee and IDP movements

details.description: This project provides a systematic model-agnostic framework for structuring the prediction problem of refugee and IDP movements. It aims to facilitate a more comprehensive understanding of this emerging field of research for humanitarian aid agencies.
details.testimonial: The field of predictive analytics for humanitarian response is still at a nascent stage, but due to growing operational and policy interest we expect that it will expand substantially in the coming years. In the course of preparing this framework, we have found that relatively little is known about the structure of this prediction problem at the high level, and that there are a number of big-picture questions for which we lack empirical evidence, such as: how far in advance displacement can be predicted; how much data is needed to train effective models; and whether models transfer across borders and humanitarian settings. We hope that this framework will help to encourage future research on these questions; facilitate comparisons between existing models; and spark a broader discussion on best practices for predicting forced displacement.

title: Big data and AI for Poverty/Vulnerability Mapping in Cambodia

details.description:
Cambodia has made substantial progress in reducing poverty in recent years, with the goal to eradicate extreme poverty by 2030. The poverty rate has decreased from 26.3 percent in 2014 to 17.8 percent in 2019 (MoP, 2021). Nevertheless, significant segments of the population remain vulnerable to economic shocks and setbacks, the latest being the COVID-19 pandemic which has reversed the country's development gains to the 2018 level. The reduction of multidimensional poverty in Cambodia continues to be on positive trend despite health and economic shocks in recent years. The latest global Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) report, published by UNDP and the University of Oxford in 2023, indicates that the incidence of multidimensional poverty in Cambodia fell from 36.7 percent to 16.6 percent. 

To address the challenges of poverty eradication, access to periodic and timely data is crucial. UNDP have embraced advancements in technology, particularly in Artificial Intelligence (AI), to develop the Cambodia Poverty/Vulnerability Mapping tool. This tool combines traditional and big data sources to provide a multidimensional perspective on poverty and vulnerability in Cambodia. By integrating different datasets, policymakers can identify patterns and interactions that are often overlooked when studying poverty separately. The tool allows users to explore poverty vulnerability alongside specific indicators such as education, health, living standards, and monetary factors at various geographic levels. The tool is now transferred to the National Institute of Statistics.

title: Project Jetson

details.description:
Project Jetson (2017-2021) was a predictive analytics experiment to discover, understand, and measure the specific push and pull factors that cause, indicate or exacerbate the forced displacement. Project Jetson gives UNHCR and other humanitarian organizations the potential to become more proactive in their contingency planning, emergency preparedness and response efforts, a transformation that could significantly improve on-the-ground relief services and more importantly the lives of those who are forcibly displaced.

Humanitarian challenge Drought exacerbating internal displacement in Somalia generated by protracted conflict. 

Challenge Question How might UNHCR predict the number of people arriving into the different regions of Somalia?

The variables selected in Jetson, represent some of the most important influencing factors for forced displacement in the operational context of Somalia. The variables were selected according to different assumptions we needed to later validate, even from qualitative data or quantitative ground truth data. For selecting variables and validating them, we used several innovation methodologies,
details.ai_approach: Predictive Analytics: Classical Machine-Learning (ML) models for Time Series Analysis (TSA) e.g. XgBoost, Decision-trees, etc. Tried Neural Networks, but given gaps in data collection (e.g., conflict areas) was not sucessful

title: Local AI Language Accelerator Programme

details.description:
Artificial intelligence, especially natural language-based technologies, have emerged as a transformative tool for sustainable development, creating new opportunities to foster inclusion and drive social and economic growth. However, not all societies can benefit from this innovation equally: many linguistic communities are underrepresented online and therefore face major hurdles in fully harnessing the benefits of AI innovation. 

UNDP’s Local Language Accelerator Programme aims to make the benefits of AI available to diverse populations regardless of the language they speak. In collaboration with technical and academic partners, it tackles key hurdles that limit the potential of low-resource language AI ecosystems and burden new AI start-ups: lack of data, extractive data economies, unsustainable funding, and limited opportunities for cross-sector and cross-border collaboration. The Programme’s country implementations support the creation of high-quality, accessible voice or text datasets in local languages to ensure that these resources are available for entrepreneurs to create AI solutions which are representative, accurate, and available to speakers of local or Indigenous languages. It also pilots community-driven platforms, frameworks and data licenses designed to ensure proper consent, robust data provenance, and continued community benefit – including support for local start-ups active across various domains. To reinforce this practical work, UNDP also prioritises global and regional advocacy to increase inter-institutional collaboration and support for the digitalisation of local languages in cross-border linguistic communities, fostering a collaborative ecosystem that encourages stakeholders from government, academia, the private sector, and civil society to actively contribute to the development and maintenance of inclusive and context-responsive AI solutions, systems and digital infrastructures. 

Goal: The programme will accelerate the digitization of low-resource languages through a globally replicable methodology enabled by responsible and scalable partnership models. It will support the reach, relevance and safety of existing AI models and pilot community-led data solutions to catalyse new Language AI innovation and expand the availability of AI technologies for start-ups, public administration, and other stakeholders. 

How countries can engage: Collaborate to identify high-impact use-cases for Language AI and accelerate the digital inclusion of local language speakers. Establish local, regional and global partnerships for local language digitization. Leverage the methodology for digitizing local languages (being developed). Leverage the global partner base and Expert Group for access to expertise, compute, and data (being developed).

title: AI Landscape Monitor

details.description:
Landscape Monitor is a dynamic knowledge-mapping tool designed to track and visualize the evolving landscape of artificial intelligence (AI) developments. It aggregates, organizes, and presents information on emerging technologies, research trends, and use cases, enabling stakeholders to stay informed and make strategic decisions. The platform emphasizes interactivity, timeliness, and contextual insights, making it ideal for monitoring complex, fast-changing domains. 

Adaptability Beyond AI:
While designed for AI, the underlying architecture - data aggregation, classification, and visualization - can be adapted to other domains such as: 
Climate Change Monitoring: Track policies, technologies, and global initiatives.
Public Health Surveillance: Map disease outbreaks, interventions, and research.
Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs): Monitor progress and innovations across targets.
details.ai_approach: It augments GenAI with search capabilities.  Its adaptable architecture, built on a robust API layer and a React.js frontend, makes it suitable not only for AI monitoring but also for critical areas such as climate change, public health, and SDG progress tracking. This flexibility ensures that institutions can leverage the same technology to drive evidence-based policy, accelerate innovation, and enhance global collaboration.
details.testimonial: This tool acts as a strategic intelligence platform, enabling organizations to anticipate trends, identify gaps, and make informed decisions in any complex domain.

title: The Mediterranean and Pan-European Forecast and Early Warning System against Natural Hazards (MedEWSa) project

details.description: MedEWSa is an Innovation action (IA) project led by the Justus Liebig University Giessen (JLU) and a consortium of 30 partners. Building on existing tools, MedEWSa will develop a fully integrated impact-based multi-hazard early warning system (EWS). It will achieve advances beyond the state-of-the-art in the areas of AI-based decision support solutions for improved impact prediction, methods for impact prediction and early warnings, modelling and prediction of multiple hazard dynamics and their interdependencies. MedEWSa will explore hybrid methods combining data-driven approaches and the laws of physics, using tools learned from observations and physics-based model results. Ultimately, it will deploy an analysis to provide integrated, accurate, and rapid early warnings for the pan-European-Mediterranean-African region. MedEWSa will directly contribute to the United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goals and align with the UN’s Early Warnings for All initiative. The project will also develop innovative financial solutions through risk transfer to capital markets. MedEWSa will also set out a roadmap for contributing to different standardisation activities to identify significant opportunities to push contributions into future standards, pre-normative activities, and open collaborative development environments.
details.region_names: Europe and the Commonwealth of Independent States
details.testimonial: The MedEWSa was launched in November 2023. The MedEWSa project emphasizes the importance of research and multi-stakeholder collaboration in enhancing Mediterranean and European countries' operational EWS capabilities. It aims to enhance collaboration, research, innovation, and the dissemination of knowledge and technologies in support of EU policies addressing global challenges.

title: SKAI: AI-Powered Satellite Imagery for Disaster Response

details.description: WFP, in collaboration with Google Research, has developed SKAI, an AI-powered satellite imagery analysis tool that significantly accelerates disaster damage assessments. Using advanced machine learning, SKAI automates the identification of damaged buildings and infrastructure, providing critical insights in under 48 hours, 13 times faster and 77 percent cheaper than manual methods. In crises such as the Türkiye-Syria earthquakes and Pakistan floods, SKAI supported rapid assessments, enabling faster, more efficient humanitarian responses. By reducing reliance on manual analysis, the tool ensures that WFP and its partners can quickly determine the extent of damage, prioritize assistance, and allocate resources effectively.

title: Croatia Business Environment Reform with applied AI

details.description: The World Bank has been supporting the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development (MoESD) of Croatia in digitalizing Government to Business (G2B) service delivery for business registration and business licensing. This advisory work is carried out by the Bank at the request of the Government, with funding by the European Union, and in cooperation with the European Commission's DG REFORM. The work involved piloting an innovative approach for mapping business administrative procedures that involved the application of AI/Machine Learning (ML) and Natural Language Processing (NLP). The developed digital algorithm processed 110 laws and 1,204 bylaws from the registry of regulations to identify more than 9,000 potential regulatory requirements in 33 administrative areas, including business authorizations (permits, licenses, etc.), and minimum conditions. Further, the data cleansing resulted in a mapping database of ~1,500 business-related administrative procedures. The Bank also produced a report on recommendations for publishing the mapping online and on a mechanism to keep the mapping data updated following regulatory changes, and a roadmap for modernization and digitalization of Government to Business (G2B) service delivery.

title: Tech-facilitated gender-based violence in the Caribbean: Perception and Awareness of AI-based Discrimination among Women and Girls in the Caribbean

details.description:
As Artificial Intelligence (AI) becomes more integrated into daily life, biases embedded in AI systems pose a growing risk of exacerbating gender inequalities and leaving women behind. Furthermore, the underrepresentation of women in AI development and leadership deepens these challenges and reinforces stereotypes.  

In 2024, UNESCO in collaboration with the Caribbean Sheroes Alumni network conducted a regional survey covering the English and Dutch-speaking Caribbean called “Perception and Awareness of AI Discrimination Among Women and Girls in the Caribbean” exploring: 

• The perceptions of discrimination by AI algorithms 
• The awareness of potential biases within AI affecting Caribbean women and girls 
• Knowledge of AI’s broader impacts on Caribbean society.

An important objective is to understand what complementary investments ensure that the benefits of AI are widely shared rather than concentrated among a few. In support of these goals, we are convening an interdisciplinary community of researchers, AI experts, and policy makers who are committed to using AI to advance the World Bank’s mission of ending poverty and boosting shared prosperity on a livable planet.

title: AI Job Description Generator

details.description:
The AI Job Description Suite accelerates recruitment content creation and refinement through two complementary modules: (1) the AI Job Description Generator, which produces market-aligned, structured job descriptions from minimal inputs and templates; and (2) the Job Description Enhancer, which upgrades existing postings by enriching responsibilities, qualifications, KPIs, and language quality to improve clarity, competitiveness, and candidate appeal.

The suite integrates template parsing, AI-powered content generation, and real-time market terminology alignment. Users can upload organizational templates (.md, .txt, .pdf) to preserve standards (e.g., “About Us,” “Competencies,” “How to Apply”) and generate both a full job description and a concise Core Elements summary. 
Outputs are downloadable in Markdown and Word (.docx) formats, and the UI provides step-by-step progress, preview tabs, and model selection (OpenAI or Gemini). 

A human-in-the-loop workflow ensures all AI-generated content remains editable and under expert control, maintaining governance and organizational voice consistency while reducing manual drafting time.

title: Brazil Justica 4.0

details.description:
The “Justiça 4.0” Program launched four new AI models for classifying court cases, contributing to the reduction of trial time and the number of appeals in the Brazilian courts. The platform integrates AI to streamline judicial processes, support decision-making, and foster innovation within Brazil's judiciary.

PEDRO (Court Precedents Extraction and Discovery Platform): Developed in partnership with the University of Brasília (UnB), the model infers, from the initial petitions, the qualified precedents of the Federal Supreme Court (STF) and the Superior Court of Justice (STJ), also showing the degree of similarity with the analyzed case. 

KAIROS (K-Means Clustering Similarity for Legal Documents): Groups processes using an unsupervised machine learning method and can be used to manage the collection of processes and classify them by subject, branch, among others. It is the result of a partnership with the Federal University of Goiás (UFG). 

ALICIA (Linguistic Analysis for Automated Classification): Developed in partnership with the University of Fortaleza (Unifor), it promotes assignment of subjects based on Unified Procedural Tables. 

ANA (Automated Standards Analysis): Model trained for retrieving legal texts and associated jurisprudential precedents, developed with Unifor. 

Key AI functionalities encompass automated data extraction from legal documents, classification of legal matters, and identification of relevant precedents, thereby reducing manual workload and expediting case analysis. By leveraging machine learning algorithms and natural language processing, the Gabinete do Juízo facilitates more accurate and timely judicial decisions, contributing to a more accessible and effective justice system.

title: UNHCR Global AI Approach: Vision

details.description:
UNHCR’s AI Approach provides a strategic framework for using artificial intelligence in humanitarian contexts.

Rooted in human rights and humanitarian principles, it aims to improve outcomes for forcibly displaced and stateless people through responsible, inclusive, and transparent AI deployment.

What safeguards are in place to ensure ethical AI use?
UNHCR’s AI Approach is a model for ethical innovation in humanitarian work. It ensures that technology serves people, not the other way around, delivering faster, fairer, and more effective support to those in need.

What safeguards are in place to ensure ethical AI use?
- Ethical and human rights-based. This foundation ensures that AI adoption strengthens protection outcomes while safeguarding the rights and dignity of displaced and stateless populations
- Embrace AI responsibility by design. Maintaining the integrity of AI-assisted processes is essential to upholding the trust placed in UNHCR and ensuring institutional accountability.
- Champion people-centred AI. Human centricity is being embedded into the core of all AI initiatives, through the testing of new products with communities, designing different human centered processes, a commitment to shifting power dynamics, or adapting proven approaches to fit local needs and realities.
- Ensure robust internal governance. UNHCR’s governance of AI is being built on existing institutional processes and established decision-making structures.
- Foster meaningful partnerships. UNHCR’s engagement in AI is driven by strong collaboration across a diverse range of partners, including governments, international institutions and other UN agencies.

How does UNHCR advocate and engage on responsible AI?
- UNHCR is actively engaging in global conversations to promote the ethical use of artificial intelligence in humanitarian contexts.
- The organization advocates for AI systems that are rights-based, inclusive, transparent and accountable.

title: Agentic Academic Paper Review System

details.description: **The Agentic Academic Review System** is an automated, multi-agent AI framework designed to evaluate large volumes of academic papers with customizable precision. It enables users to define bespoke review criteria and leverages a structured team of AI agents —Specialist, Editor, and Judge— to perform detailed assessments, synthesize findings, and adjudicate discrepancies across different model outputs. The system supports batch processing of hundreds of documents, generates markdown reviews and CSV reports, and allows for comparative analysis between AI models. Users can tailor agent behavior, scoring scales, and domain specialization through editable YAML and prompt files, without modifying core code. With modular architecture and support for multiple LLM providers, the tool offers scalable, transparent, and reproducible academic review workflows, ideal for researchers, institutions, and editorial teams seeking to enhance review efficiency and consistency.
details.technology_platform:
Core Language Models (LLMs):
OpenAI GPT family (e.g., GPT-4o-mini, GPT-5)
DeepSeek models (e.g., deepseek-reasoner, deepseek-chat)
Anthropic Claude (e.g., claude-haiku-4-5, claude-sonnet-4-5)
Google Gemini (e.g., gemini-2.5-pro for Judge role)
Frameworks & Tools:
Python-based orchestration scripts
Pydantic for schema validation
YAML for criteria configuration


Environment & Integration:

.env for API keys and model endpoints
Supports custom endpoints for proprietary models
details.ai_approach:
Academic Paper Review – Adjudication Framework
Agentic Workflow

Specialist Agent: Evaluates each criterion (multi-pass), outputs scores + direct quotes.
Editor Agent: Synthesizes specialist outputs into a coherent review and weighted score (0–100).
Judge Agent: Resolves conflicts between model outputs with rationale.
Human Reviewer (Mandatory): Final decision authority; validates evidence and signs off.


Adjudication Process

Initial AI Review: Specialist + Editor produce structured reviews.
Conflict Detection: Triggered by score/recommendation variance or missing evidence.
AI Judge: Issues reconciliation verdict with reasoning.
Human Adjudication: Reviews all AI outputs, verifies evidence, and makes the final decision.


Core Principles

Prompt Engineering: Separate system prompts (role definition) and user prompts (task instructions).
Evaluation Strategy: Weighted scoring (100-point scale), evidence-based outputs with direct quotes.
Customization: Criteria, weights, and tone via YAML and editable prompts.
Scalability: Batch processing, run directories, parallel execution, resume capability.
Governance: All AI outputs are advisory; human review is strictly required.

AI was also a central theme during the UN SDG:Learn Retreat in November 2024, where partners engaged in strategic discussions on the future of AI in learning, including its potential to transform instructional design and learner engagement.
In addition, the UN SDG:Learn podcast featured a thematic episode titled “Banking on Biodiversity: The Seed Saver’s Crusade”, which explored how artificial intelligence and digital tools can support biodiversity, local knowledge systems, and sustainable agriculture. In the episode, Stefan Schmitz, Executive Director of the Global Crop Diversity Trust, emphasized the role of AI and data mining in advancing modern breeding technologies and reviving neglected crops. This episode illustrates the intersection of AI, local innovation, and the SDGs—broadening the scope of sustainable development learning by linking digital innovation with global food systems and biodiversity preservation.

title: AI-powered multidimensional vulnerability mapping tool for early warning system

details.description:
Southeast Asia faces annual disaster-related economic losses of nearly $54 billion, with over 165 million people highly vulnerable to climate and socio-economic shocks. While hazard data (e.g., wildfire, drought, flooding) has advanced significantly through remote sensing and climate models, vulnerability data — poverty, housing quality, education, access to markets, health risks — remains outdated, fragmented, or unavailable at granular scales. Conventional surveys cannot capture fast-changing dynamics in conflict, food insecurity, or wildfire exposure.
The result: governments especially in Cambodia and humanitarian actors struggle to identify at-risk populations in real time, often intervening too late or missing marginalized groups.

This initiative fills that gap by building a generative AI-powered platform to map and monitor multidimensional vulnerability in near real time, transforming static data into actionable intelligence.

It will also integrate an AI-powered chatbot capable of answering queries such as how many schools and hospitals are affected by PM2.5 in Phnom Penh, and where they are located, among others. The broader goal is to inspire broader adoption across institutions, so knowledge sharing is also a key component of the project.

title: Data Visualization Suite

details.description: The Data Visualization Suite is an advanced platform for transforming structured and unstructured data into actionable insights through generative AI-driven visualization and storytelling tools.
details.technology_platform: Built on a ReactJS frontend and a Python backend, the platform integrates advanced graph libraries for dynamic rendering and supports multiple Generative AI models, including OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek, and Ollama for enhanced privacy and control, while giving users the flexibility to bring their own API keys for seamless customization.
details.ai_approach:
The suite consists of five core components:
1. Data Analytics and Visualization Tool – Focused on structured data, this module allows users to design and refine analysis plans using one generative AI model, then generate visualizations with another. Users can experiment with different model combinations, save their preferred outputs, and later fuse or mix-and-match charts using the Chart Manager for comprehensive dashboards.

2. Chart Manager – Provides an intuitive interface to combine, customize, and harmonize multiple charts into cohesive, interactive dashboards, enabling flexible reporting and presentation.

3. Infographics Generator – Designed for unstructured data, such as academic papers or reports. It extracts key insights and produces visual elements summarizing main points. Users can select different generative AI models to create varied outputs, which can then serve as inputs for the Infographics Manager.

4. Infographics Manager – Aggregates and merges outputs from multiple infographic runs, combining visual elements and textual summaries into a unified, polished presentation.

5. Mind Map Generator – Converts hierarchical or conceptual data into interactive branching diagrams, supporting brainstorming and knowledge organization.

By leveraging multiple generative AI models across structured and unstructured data workflows, this suite empowers users to create dynamic, multi-layered visual narratives that enhance decision-making and communication.

title: Automatic Loan Approval and Gender Bias in SME Lending

details.description: This project examines whether automatic credit approval can reduce gender bias in SME lending. We collaborated with a bank in Peru that piloted a new screening tool to generate psychometric credit scores. Applicants who scored above a predefined threshold were automatically offered a loan with a size tied to their score, while those below the threshold were assessed by a loan officer. Using a regression discontinuity design and credit bureau data, we compare loan offers and loan sizes of women and men applicants within a narrow window around the automatic approval threshold. The results show that women applicants below the threshold are less likely to take out loans and receive smaller loan amounts than men. However, this gender bias disappears for applicants above the threshold, suggesting that automated screening methods than can reduce loan officer discretion and promote gender equity in lending. This project is part of the research program of the AI/DD Research Initiative at the Development Research Group.

title: Baro Note: AI Meeting Assistant for Knowledge Management

details.description:
Activity Objectives
Baro Note is designed to strengthen knowledge management maturity across UNDP and partner institutions by enabling automated capture, structuring, and utilization of meeting-driven knowledge assets. The core objectives of the activity are:
1. To establish an AI-enabled system capable of recording, transcribing, organizing and summarizing spoken content generated during meetings, interviews, workshops, and field discussions.
2. To significantly reduce the time and manual effort required for documentation by automating real-time speech recognition, summarization, translation, and action item extraction.
3. To enhance accessibility and inclusivity of organizational knowledge by supporting transcription, translation, and summarization in more than 40 languages, reducing losses caused by linguistic and operational barriers.
4. To enable knowledge augmentation using Large Language Models (LLMs), allowing users to derive insights, extract themes, and connect information across multiple discussions and data sources.
5. To position Baro Note as a foundational component of sustainable digital knowledge infrastructure within UNDP, aligned with Digital Public Infrastructure and AI-for-Development principles.
6. To explore the integration of open-source and on-premise language models, as well as edge-device deployment, in order to strengthen data security, support digital sovereignty, and ensure adaptability across diverse operational environments.

Expected Impact
Baro Note acts not only as a productivity tool, but as an enabler of cultural transformation in how knowledge is captured, shared, and utilized across the organization. The expected impact includes:
1. A projected 60–80 percent reduction in time spent producing meeting minutes and documentation, enabling staff to focus on strategic and value-adding tasks.
2. Improved transparency, accountability, and traceability in decision-making processes through standardized and consistent documentation practices.
3. Greater inclusivity and knowledge equity by enabling non-English-speaking colleagues, government partners, and stakeholders to equally access and contribute to institutional knowledge.
4. Strengthened organizational learning through the accumulation and reuse of structured knowledge, reducing duplication and fragmentation across projects and teams.
5. Enhanced trust and compliance through deployment options supporting local hosting and secure model execution, making the tool suitable for government counterparts and sensitive environments.
6. Direct alignment with UNDP’s digital transformation agenda, creating pathways for scale, cost-efficiency, and potential evolution into a Digital Public Good supporting replication across regions and partner governments.

title: Multi-agent Multi-model Deep Research System

details.description:
A multi-agent, multi-model system designed to automate the end-to-end process of deep research and report generation. The system addresses the traditionally labor-intensive and time-consuming nature of knowledge synthesis by orchestrating a sequential, human-in-the-loop workflow. 

The architecture comprises a Planning Agent, which deconstructs a high-level user topic into a structured, editable research plan, and a Research Agent, which executes this plan by performing deep web research for each subtopic. 

It addresses the limitations of traditional research workflows, which often suffer from algorithmic bias and informational silos, by leveraging multi-engine synthesis and an AI Judge to produce high-fidelity insights. The system ensures objectivity by comparing outputs from different search engines and consolidating them into a single, superior report.

Key Features:

Automated Planning: Breaks down topics into objectives and subtopics.
Deep Web Research: Executes multi-engine searches for broad coverage.
Cited Synthesis: Produces structured reports with references.
AI Judging: Compares multiple drafts and merges the best insights.
Automated Scoring: Quantifies report quality based on coverage and depth.
Iteration Tools: Allows re-synthesis without re-running full research.

Value Proposition:

Delivers comprehensive, unbiased, and actionable research outputs that surpass single-source approaches, making it ideal for academic, policy, and enterprise use cases.

Adaptability Beyond Research:

This architecture can be repurposed for other domains:
Policy Analysis: Aggregate and synthesize legislative data.
Market Intelligence: Compare insights from multiple industry sources.
Risk Assessment: Merge reports from different compliance engines.
details.technology_platform:
Frontend:

Web-based interface for topic input, plan editing, and report management.
Likely built with React.js for dynamic UI and seamless workflow visualization.


Backend:

Python-based orchestration (Flask/FastAPI) for managing research steps.
Integration with multiple search APIs (web and academic).


Data Layer:

Structured storage for research plans, citations, and synthesized reports.


Deployment:

Dockerized microservices for portability and scalability.
details.ai_approach:
Multi-Engine Strategy: Uses different search engines (web, academic) to overcome filter bubbles.
LLM-Orchestrated Workflow:
-Plan Generation Engine: Creates structured research plans.
-Search Engine Model: Executes targeted queries for each subtopic.
-Synthesis Engine: Consolidates findings into coherent, cited reports.

AI Judge:
-Compares multiple synthesized drafts, resolves contradictions, and produces a definitive version.
Scoring Utility:
-Evaluates reports against metrics like objective fulfillment, coverage, and depth.
-Iteration Capability:
Allows re-synthesis using existing data for efficiency and quality improvement.

It also features a robust citation management system, which automatically tracks sources from initial data gathering through complex synthesis stages, ensuring the integrity and verifiability of the final report. 

By orchestrating multiple specialized AI agents and models within an iterative framework, the Deep Research Agent significantly accelerates the research lifecycle, enhances the quality of synthesized reports, and provides a powerful, scalable platform for in-depth analysis.

title: AI in human resource management: The limits of empiricism

details.description:
The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into Human Resource Management (HRM) is 
transforming how organizations recruit, manage, and evaluate their workforces. While proponents champion AI as a means to enhance efficiency, reduce bias, and align HR practices with 
strategic business goals, this paper argues that such optimism is misplaced. Drawing on a critical 
review of AI's application across four core HRM functions—recruitment, compensation, scheduling, and performance management—this paper identifies significant risks and limitations arising from the fundamental structure of AI systems.
Central to the analysis is a three-parameter framework for assessing AI tools: their objective, the 
data they rely upon, and how they are programmed. The paper shows that across HR functions, 
AI systems frequently operationalize reductive or poorly aligned objectives, rely on low-quality 
or biased data, and are programmed in non-transparent ways that undermine their usefulness. 
These structural shortcomings not only undermine the effectiveness of AI systems but also introduce legal, ethical, and practical risks for firms and their workers.

It also presents reflections on how we conceptualize and practice human rights in the face of technology-driven change on a global scale. The Series was launched to coincide with the 37th Session of the UN Human Rights Council, as part of UNRISD’s commitment to promote socially just and sustainable development within and beyond the UN system. title: Supporting Member States in lmplementing UNESCO's Recommendation on the Ethics of Al through lnnovative Tools

details.description:
UNESCO aims to advance the global implementation of the Recommendation on the Ethics of AI by assisting countries in establishing robust national institutions for effective AI governance. This project, supported by the European Commission’s Directorate-General for International Partnerships, facilitates implementation of the Recommendation in the form of support for developing and implementing national policy, legislation, regulation and other governance mechanisms.

It achieves this aim by providing sustained technical assistance to countries for the effective implementation of the Recommendation, to achieve four interconnected major outcomes:
1. Beneficiary countries will build strong national institutions for promoting AI ethics via the implementation of the AI Readiness Assessment Methodology (RAM) and Ethical Impact Assessment (EIA) tool in 18 countries.
2. Countries will advance the implementation of the Recommendation on the Ethics of AI through the technical support provided by a global AI Ethics Experts Without Borders network, established and operationalised by UNESCO.
3. Judicial operators worldwide will strengthen the rule of law, democracy, and human rights based on the Recommendation and international standards for AI. 
4. High-level policy dialogue on AI will be reinforced through the annual Global Forum on the Ethics of AI, based on peer-to-peer learning and sharing best practices among governments and other AI stakeholders.

title: Care Georeferencing Tool for Inclusive Care Systems in Latin America and the Caribbean

details.description:
The Care Georeferencing Tool is an AI-powered decision-making support system designed to map the supply, demand, and accessibility gaps in care services in a selected territory. By identifying "care deserts," it helps governments target critical interventions, highlighting the needs of specific groups such as older adults, persons with disabilities, and children, who require care and support services but cannot reach them.

The tool combines traditional data with innovative AI-enabled data collection methods such as web scraping, collaborative mapping, and deep learning models that leverage satellite imagery. Additionally, it provides insights for policy formulation and resource allocation to enhance care systems inclusivity.

The tool also aims to strengthen the public digital infrastructure of countries by generating care maps and building capacities for the counterparts to sustain and scale them. Furthermore, it can interoperate with other information systems, such as those for disaster risk reduction (DRR), making it useful in disaster contexts to identify vulnerable populations and critical infrastructure.

details.description:

title: AI and Multimedia Authenticity Standards Collaboration (AMAS)

details.description:
The AI and Multimedia Authenticity Standards Collaboration (AMAS) is convened by ITU under the auspices of the World Standards Cooperation and was launched at the AI for Good Summit 2024. The AI and Multimedia Authenticity Standards Collaboration is a global, multistakeholder initiative bringing together global leaders in standards, technology, academia and policy to support the journey toward building trust in digital media. Its mission is to support those who combat malicious deepfakes, protect individual rights and help to build a future where we can trust digital content.

The main objectives of AMAS are to: 
1.	Provide a global forum for dialogue on priority topics for discussion across standards organisations in the area of AI and multimedia authenticity. 
2.	Map the landscape of technical standards for AI and multimedia authenticity including but not limited to watermarking, provenance and deepfakes detection while facilitating sharing of knowledge on lessons learned from different stakeholders. 
3.	Identify gaps where new standards are required given the fast-moving nature of the AI and multimedia authenticity landscape. 
4.	Support the policy, regulatory requirements and government policy measures with regards to AI and multimedia authenticity to facilitate transparency and legal compliance with but not limited to protection of privacy of users, authorship and the rights of owners and consumers.

More information can be obtained on the website of AMAS: https://aiforgood.itu.int/multimedia-authenticity.
details.links_resources:
AMAS launched on 11 July 2025 at the AI for Good Global Summit 2025 two groundbreaking technical and policy papers offering recommendations to guide the governance of AI globally and combat mis-and-disinformation:

1) The Technical paper offers a comprehensive overview of the current landscape of standards and specifications related to digital media authenticity and artificial intelligence. By mapping the contributions of various Standard Development Organizations (SDOs) and groups, the report aims to identify gaps and opportunities for further standardization. This could serve as a valuable resource for stakeholders seeking to navigate the complex ecosystem of standards at the intersection of artificial intelligence and authenticity in digital media and to implement best practices to safeguard the authenticity of digital assets and the rights assigned to them.

2) The Policy paper provides policymakers with guidance on how to leverage international standards for the effective regulation of the creation, use and dissemination of synthetic multimedia content. The report offers practical guidance and actionable recommendations, including a regulatory options matrix designed to help policymakers and regulators determine what to regulate (scope), how to regulate (voluntary or mandatory mechanisms), and to what extent (level of effort). It also explores a range of supporting tools – such as standards, conformity assessment mechanisms, and enabling technologies – that can contribute to addressing the challenges of misinformation and disinformation arising from the misuse of multimedia content. It includes a set of practical checklists for use by policymakers, regulators, and technology providers. These can be used when designing regulations or enforcement frameworks, developing technological solutions, or preparing crisis response strategies. The checklists are intended to help align stakeholder expectations, identify critical gaps, support responsible innovation, and enable conformity with emerging standards and best practices.

The two AMAS reports can be accessed here: https://aiforgood.itu.int/multimedia-authenticity/#reports

title: Mini portable X-ray Machines Equipped with AI technology

details.description: In partnership with UNDP Morocco’s Accelerator Lab and Morocco’s Central Bank, ICPSD SDG Reaching vulnerable population in remote outer islands and many islets is challenging in the PICs. Currently, the presumptive TB patients are referred to main island for Xray. During this referral a good number of cases do not seek diagnosis and the program lose many presumptive cases. The available X-ray is bulky and carrying it to the outer islands in small boats is a huge challenge. Hence, a portable Xray machine is required to help the program in diagnosing the TB cases on the spot and immediate initiation of treatment for active TB case. One such innovation is the mini portable x-ray machine, equipped with advanced artificial intelligence (AI)-powered software. Under the C19RM grant, the Federated States of Micronesian, Kiribati, Palau, Republic of Marshall Islands, Samoa, Tonga, Tuvalu and Vanuatu have recently received Portable X-Ray Instrument equipped with CAD software (AI). These compact devices can fit in a suitcase and be carried by a single technician to the most remote communities outside of the reach of health care services and produce rapid, accurate results, without the need for on-site radiologists.  This initiative will help to reach our ultimate objective of ending TB in the Pacific and beyond by 2030.

title: Global case studies of social dialogue on AI and algorithmic management

details.description: Employers are adopting and refining artificial intelligence (AI) and algorithm-based tools in the workplace, with wide-ranging implications for work and employment. This working paper examines case studies of social dialogue on AI at national, regional, sectoral, company, and workplace levels in Europe, North America, Asia, South America and the Caribbean, and Africa. Findings are organized around three distinct ‘action fields’ in which worker representatives have sought to influence strategies and outcomes associated with the growing use of AI and algorithms in the workplace. These include the employment and skill impacts of AI, algorithmic management practices, and working conditions and rights in AI value chains. Across these action fields, social dialogue is playing a crucial role in encouraging an alternative, high road approach to AI investments and uses, based on complementing rather than replacing worker skills, empowering rather than controlling the workforce, and embedding rather than displacing new jobs in labor and social protections. Comparative findings suggest that these social dialogue initiatives are more effective where there are constraints on employer exit, support for collective worker voice, and strategies of inclusive labor solidarity.

details.description: This project is a collaboration between UNU-WIDER and the African Center for Economic Transformation (ACET). It focuses on enhancing the Ghanaian tax-benefit microsimulation model (GHAMOD), a tool used for analysing the distributional and budgetary impacts of fiscal policies. title: Digital Technologies, Hiring, Training, and Firm Outcomes: Evidence from AI and ICT Adoption in Indian firms

details.description: In this study, using a novel dataset that matches firm-level data with online job vacancy data, we investigate the effects of firms’ digital technology adoption on future hiring and the dynamics of hiring and training, focusing on different types of technologies and categories of occupations. First, we examine the impact of adopting different types of digital technologies, namely AI, Advanced ICT, and Basic ICT, on future firm hiring. Second, we show that there is a positive relationship between training and new hiring only for one occupational category, namely, managers, with no significant relationship for other occupations. Third, we investigate the joint effect of training and technology adoption for firm performance. Our findings reveal that digital technology adoption enhances a firm’s financial performance only when combined with internal staff training. The sole exception is AI, which yields positive performance benefits even in the absence of training.

title: EnvironmentGPT

details.description:
1. What is EnvironmentGPT?

EnvironmentGPT is UNEP’s first public beta chatbot designed to make trusted environmental science easier to access. Built on a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture, it provides accurate, cited answers drawn exclusively from UNEP-approved publications. Unlike general-purpose AI models trained on open internet data, EnvironmentGPT ensures transparency, scientific integrity, and reduced hallucinations. Future versions will be integrated into UNEP’s World Environment Situation Room (WESR).

2. Why It Was Built

UNEP’s mandate includes strengthening the science–policy interface. Policymakers, practitioners, and the public need rapid access to reliable environmental knowledge, yet information remains fragmented and complex to navigate. EnvironmentGPT helps bridge this gap by enabling users to:
- Summarize large volumes of information quickly
- Receive explanations tailored to different expertise levels
- Integrate knowledge across climate, biodiversity, pollution, water, land, health, and economic domains
-Access referenced, authoritative content in accessible formats

General-purpose LLMs cannot be assumed reliable for technical environmental topics; EnvironmentGPT offers a domain-specific, retrieval-based alternative aligned with UNEP’s priorities on climate stability, healthy ecosystems, and pollution reduction.

3. What Documents It Uses

The knowledge base is built using a three-tier selection framework prioritizing high-consensus global assessments, authoritative UN-led publications, and high-quality regional or peer-reviewed literature. Over 220 validated reports form the initial corpus, including:

- GEO-7
- Emissions & Adaptation Gap Reports
- Frontiers Reports
- IPCC & IPBES summaries
- Relevant FAO, WHO, and other UN publications
- Selected open-access scientific meta-analyses and systematic reviews

All documents were reviewed by UNEP’s Office of Science to ensure quality and thematic coherence.

4. Key Features

- Latest UNEP flagship assessments integrated from launch
- Filtering by publication or publication series
- Audience modes: Public, Policymaker, Scientist
- Multiple LLM options with sustainability profiles
- Confidence score based on breadth of supporting evidence
- Environmental impact metrics (energy, water, emissions, minerals per query), using EcoLogits
- Conversation memory for follow-up questions
- Full reference transparency

Improved AI environmental impact assessments

title: Solutions Radar on Justice, Security and Resilient Institutions for Development

details.description:
The Solutions Radar is an interactive UNDP platform designed to identify, analyze, and amplify innovative solutions emerging from countries across Latin America and the Caribbean. Its objective is to facilitate knowledge-sharing and accelerate the impact and quality of public policy design, implementation, and evaluation processes.

The platform aims to strengthen comprehensive responses in key rule of law areas — including security, justice, and social cohesion — in a context marked by multiple crises and digital transition.

Grounded in a people-centered approach and focused on scaling regional knowledge, the Solutions Radar promotes collaborative processes that integrate the voices, expertise, and experiences of stakeholders across the security and justice ecosystem at national and local levels — including public officials, youth, women, Afro-descendant and Indigenous peoples, academia, civil society, and the private sector.

The platform also integrates (JUSTINE), an AI-powered assistant designed to provide immediate analytical support to technical teams and counterparts. The chatbot supports context analysis, strategic intervention design, and identification of good practices. Integrated into the platform, it helps users navigate complex governance challenges and accelerate solutions aligned with the Global Programme on Rule of Law and Human Rights in Latin America and the Caribbean. Suggested prompts are included to enhance strategic use and evidence-based decision-making.

This product reflects the joint efforts of the Democratic Governance, Gender Equality, Digital Transformation, and Prosperity teams at the UNDP Regional Hub for Latin America and the Caribbean, with special recognition to Country Offices whose daily leadership and proximity to territories make tangible impact possible.

details.description: We’ve developed an AI summarization tool using Microsoft Azure OpenAI for the United Nations’ Central Emergency Response Fund (CERF). title: INFORM-Warning

details.description:
INFORM is a multi-stakeholder forum for developing shared, quantitative analysis relevant to humanitarian crises and disasters. INFORM is developing a suite of quantitative, analytical products to support decision-making at different stages of the crisis management cycle. INFORM-Warning seeks to make a contribution to the better use of data to anticipate, prevent, and respond to climate and complex risks in fragile and crisis-affected settings. The objective of INFORM-Warning is to present reliable, quantified, multi- hazard information that warns about risk trends, forecasts, scenarios and events that could lead to crisis impacts in the next 12 months and can be easily used to support decisions on preparedness and anticipatory action. The INFORM Warning system is unique as an open-source aggregator of existing early warning data sources that simplifies and interprets quantitative data to understand early warning trends.

The INFORM Warning system is structured into two complementary components: the Risk Monitor module for generating early warnings through quantitative data analysis, and the Crisis Anticipation module, an innovative AI-enhanced layer powered by Large Language Models.

The system is built primarily in Python, PostgreSQL and REST API, which serves as the backbone for the Risk Monitor module - the component responsible for generating quantitative early warnings. The system makes extensive use of advanced numerical and statistical libraries for data modeling and processing, as well as web scraping tools and APIs that automatically collect data from authoritative datasets. It also connects to humanitarian data platforms (i.e. ReliefWeb) to access reports, assessments, and other specialized datasets produced by partners and experts.

The Crisis Anticipation module adds an AI-assisted layer relying on Large Language Models (LLMs), which handle natural language understanding and summarization. Together, these components draw from cutting-edge multi-hazard forecasting datasets and text information streams, combining them to produce integrated, evidence-based early warnings with quantified crisis anticipation outputs.

The AI-enhanced methodology combines quantitative risk modeling with data mining and advanced natural language processing, creating a hybrid system that can both signal emerging risks and investigate on their measurable humanitarian impact.
At its core, the Risk Monitor relies on numerical estimation techniques and statistical models to process multi-hazard forecast data. It uses aggregation methods that combine different hazard indicators into unified warning signals and relies on time-series analysis and threshold-based alerting to identify when unanticipated risks may arise.

The Crisis Anticipation module complements this by providing quantified outputs through Large Language Models. When a warning is issued, the system automatically analyses news feeds and humanitarian reports to extract country- and crisis-specific quantitative insights, then compares those findings with the Risk Monitor’s outputs. This allows it to assess whether the predicted risks align with on-the-ground developments or if discrepancies are emerging.

details.ai_approach:
The AI-enhanced methodology combines quantitative risk modeling with data mining and advanced natural language processing, creating a hybrid system that can both signal emerging risks and investigate on their measurable humanitarian impact.

At its core, the Risk Monitor relies on numerical estimation techniques and statistical models to process multi-hazard forecast data. It uses aggregation methods that combine different hazard indicators into unified warning signals and relies on time-series analysis and threshold-based alerting to identify when unanticipated risks may arise.

The Crisis Anticipation module complements this by providing quantified outputs through Large Language Models. When a warning is issued, the system automatically analyses news feeds and humanitarian reports to extract country- and crisis-specific quantitative insights, then compares those findings with the Risk Monitor’s outputs. This allows it to assess whether the predicted risks align with on-the-ground developments or if discrepancies are emerging.

The most innovative aspect of this approach is how the LLM-based agent synthesizes information to produce measurable, forward-looking outcomes:
1. Contextual insight - analyzing historical trends and field reports to build a deeper understanding of the situation and extract crisis-specific parameters
2. Quantified crisis projections - utilizing scenario-building to provide measurable outcomes for anticipatory action. The system extracts quantitative insights from unstructured text sources to feed future crisis scenario simulations. Projected impacts are directly communicated as a quantified forecast of the crisis’s likely evolution under various scenarios, enabling evidence-based anticipatory action based on a data-driven forecast of future humanitarian needs.

This multi-modal approach constitutes a major step forward for early warning systems: it cross-validates data-driven predictions against experts’ reports and newspaper articles while transforming qualitative analysis into quantified projections that directly inform anticipatory action.

title: Responsible Artificial Intelligence Innovation in Law Enforcement

details.description:
UNICRI has established a partnership with INTERPOL to create a unique global forum to discuss the advancements and impact of using AI for law enforcement. Following the release of the “Toolkit for Responsible Artificial Intelligence Innovation in Law Enforcement”, UNICRI set out to further advance the responsible use of AI in law enforcement by supporting agencies to operationalize the guidance contained in the AI Toolkit and ensure that the AI Toolkit remains a contemporary and relevant instrument for law enforcement. This led to the launch of the next phase of work entitled “AI-POL: Advancing Innovation, Governance and Responsible AI in Law Enforcement” funded by the European Union and implemented in partnership with INTERPOL, which target efforts at the executive levels of law enforcement agencies on the issue of responsible AI, as well as the development of best practices policy approaches for selected use-cases, the convening of thematic working group meetings, and the organization of a public engagement campaign.

It is essential to work with law enforcement directly to identify their needs and help them fill their gaps in a practical and operationally oriented manner. Engagement of senior leadership in agencies is required to ensure agencies can build upon the guidance in the AI Toolkit and integrate AI responsibly. Additional targeted guidance and support is required to ensure agencies can fully understand the translation of the guidance contained in the AI Toolkit into operational settings.

title: Enhancing Self-Reliance and Preparedness for Forced Displacement in the Great Lakes Region

details.description: Project Component 2 ("Forecasting population movements for forced displacement preparedness") Developed AI models predicting the number of refugees entering Uganda from South Sudan and DRC 4-to-6 months in advance at over 80% accuracy. The performance informed a GoU request for the models to be run live and trigger disbursement of finance for the world's first displacement risk financing mechanism (the displacement crisis response mechanism (DCRM)). DCRM 1.0 released finance after per-person public service pressure levels were breached. This enabled resources to be allocated where needed most within a project lifecycle, but left host communities exposed to increased pressure while disbursement, procurement, and construction took place, straining refugee and host community relations. Prediction-based disbursement would enable capacity construction before pressure increases, when refugees arrive. It will also support humanitarian partners' planning and operations. The model ingests data representing hundreds of dimensions of 90+ variables representing change in the climate, economy, built environment, political and violence events, and online language and searches about these phenomena. Aside from high predictive accuracy, analysis of the model also identify which factors (real and perceived) were most associated with change in levels of refugee arrivals informing development and humanitarian policy and operations in DRC and South Sudan to be more precise and effective in addressing drivers of displacement.

title: AI Health Governance Tracker

details.description:
This project aims to establish a centralised, open-source repository that provides comprehensive access to legal, policy, and strategy documents on Artificial Intelligence for Health, Health Data, and Digital Health, with a strong focus on supporting Low- and Middle-Income Countries (LMICs). The platform will serve as a one-stop platform, allowing policymakers and decision-makers to easily access official documents, enable cross-country and cross-regional comparisons, and support informed analysis for evidence-based decision-making, particularly in LMICs where resources and governance frameworks may be limited. In addition to providing policies and guidelines produced by governments, regional bodies, and multilateral organisations, the repository will leverage AI-powered tools to assess alignment with global equity frameworks and evolving Health Data Governance Principles, ensuring that positioning and principles remain central to its design.

Built as a living and agile platform, the repository will be continuously and updated to include both newly published and revised legal, policy, and strategy documents as they emerge. To ensure its relevance and reliability, the initiative is coordinated by United Nations University through its International Institute for Global Health (UNU-IIGH) and Campus Computing Centre, and will invite voluntary contributions from experts and non-experts worldwide in multiple languages, with UNU-IIGH curating and validating entries.
details.technology_platform: Our platform leverages a flexible Generative AI ecosystem, orchestrating top-tier providers, such as OpenAI, Azure, Google Gemini, Anthropic Claude, Perplexity, and DeepSeek, alongside local models for full control and privacy. This multi-model architecture balances cost and accuracy by deploying lightweight models for metadata extraction and frontier reasoning engines for complex policy analysis. The Streamlit-based web interface enables iterative refinement, facilitating prompt calibration and output comparison to identify the optimal LLM provider. Airtable integration enables structured, shareable data, with flexible exports (JSON, DOCX, PDF, Markdown) for easy analysis and transparent results.  The backend is built on Python, laying the foundation for a planned batch processing phase. This upcoming capability will enable scalable operations by targeting specific directories of policy documents for automated, high-volume execution with minimal manual intervention.
details.ai_approach: Leveraging a hybrid of Generative AI and NLP, the platform transforms static policy documents into actionable insights by mapping them to recognised governance and equity frameworks. Uniquely, the system employs a strength-based evaluation model: rather than solely identifying gaps, it highlights where policies successfully reflect global principles. This positive reinforcement approach is designed to catalyse knowledge exchange and capacity building, specifically enabling policymakers in LMICs to recognise and scale their existing governance assets. The result is an objective, transparent analysis that promotes best practices while remaining sensitive to local contexts.

title: Gender Bias Overview Tool (GenBOT)

details.description:
The Gender Bias Overview Tool (GenBOT) project involved a partnership among UNICC, UNFPA, and Columbia University Capstone participants from 2024. Gender bias in datasets, particularly in the field of machine learning and AI, has been a long-standing issue. Despite efforts toward inclusivity and diversity, women remain underrepresented in various stages of tech development, leading to inherent biases in datasets. These biases perpetuate themselves in the development of machine learning models and algorithms, causing skewed or inaccurate outputs that reinforce existing gender disparities. To address this issue, UNICC collaborated with UNFPA and Columbia University (students and faculty) to develop GenBOT, an adaptable data-auditing solution that provides users insights on gender bias in their datasets through automated AI analytics. The tool aims to guide stakeholders in creating equitable, gender-inclusive technologies and services.

Context Matters: A key lesson learned was the importance of context in evaluating gender bias. The definition and scope of bias need to be carefully defined with stakeholders to ensure the tool's effectiveness. Thresholds and Metrics: Determining appropriate thresholds for gender bias detection was a significant challenge. The team used established research and studies to refine the metrics used in the tool, ensuring that they aligned with best practices. Stakeholder Collaboration: Continuous communication with stakeholders such as UNFPA and UNICC was crucial in refining the bias thresholds and understanding their specific needs for gender bias detection.

title: New Privacy Technologies for Better Data Sharing: Differentially Private Synthetic Microdata

details.description:
As part of its commitment to promoting open data and staying at the forefront of privacy technologies, UNHCR undertook a project to explore the use of synthetic data for some of the Microdata Library datasets.
Synthetic datasets are generated using randomly created dummy values that preserve the statistical properties of the original data, making them a valuable resource for research and analysis. Data security is ensured through differential privacy, a state-of-the-art privacy-enhancing technology that provides a rigorous mathematical framework for protecting sensitive information.

UNHCR found this methodology particularly beneficial when working with datasets that represent full enumerations rather than sample surveys. This approach was applied to registration data, a census-like collection that includes all displaced individuals registered with the organization, enabling its secure sharing on this platform.

Drawing from the experience gained in this project, UNHCR developed a practical guide to applying this methodology. The goal is to improve how humanitarian microdata can be shared in ways that preserve individual privacy while enabling high-utility insights.
details.domain: Differential privacy, synthetic data generation (OpenDP SmartNoise Synthesizers, using the MST Algorithm as the base synthesizer)
details.technology_platform:
Synthetic datasets were generated using software provided and maintained by OpenDP.
Specifically, the SmartNoise Synthesizer was utilized, which is part of the SmartNoise SDK: Tools for Differential Privacy on Tabular Data.

title: AI in the Classroom: Evaluating the Impact of Teacher Training on Teaching Practices and Student Outcomes

details.description: This study explores whether the use of Artificial Intelligence can enhance teaching practices and improve student learning outcomes in low- and middle-income contexts. Conducted as a field experiment at the primary school level in Lima, Peru, the study involves Grade 6 teachers participating in a structured training program designed to integrate Large Language Models into their teaching practices. Developed in close collaboration with teachers, this program is tailored to the local context to ensure relevance and practicality. The program includes an initial training session covering AI literacy, responsible use principles, and hands-on practice with real-world scenarios tailored to local educational needs. Key applications include adapting lesson plans for diverse student levels, creating curriculum-aligned assessments, and streamlining administrative tasks. In addition to evaluating the training program, the study introduces a cross-randomized design to compare two types of ongoing support provided throughout the academic year: peer-based networks and authority-led guidance. This component aims to identify which support system is more effective in promoting the adoption and sustained use of AI in teaching practices. The findings will contribute to a growing body of evidence on the potential of AI-powered tools in education, particularly in resource-constrained settings. By providing insights into effective training methodologies, support structures, and implementation strategies, the research will offer policy recommendations.

title: Who on Earth Is Using Generative AI ?

details.description: This paper leverages unconventional data, including website traffic data and Google Trends, to unveil the real-time usage patterns of generative artificial intelligence tools by individuals across countries. The paper also examines country-level factors driving the uptake and early impacts of generative artificial intelligence on online activities. Generative artificial intelligence users skew young, highly educated, and male, particularly for video generation tools, with usage patterns strongly indicating productivity-related activities. Generative artificial intelligence has achieved unprecedentedly rapid global diffusion, reaching almost all economies worldwide within 16 months of ChatGPT’s release. Middle-income economies have disproportionately high adoption of generative artificial intelligence relative to their economic scale, now contribute more than 50 percent of global traffic, while low-income economies contribute less than 1 percent. The paper emphasizes the need for targeted investments in digital infrastructure and skills development to harness the full potential of artificial intelligence.

In 2025, UNODA convened three multistakeholder exchanges to advance international discussions on the implications of artificial intelligence (AI) in the military domain for international peace and security. These explored the opportunities and risks posed by military AI, including its impact on compliance with international law, the risks of miscalculation and escalation, and the challenges of ensuring accountability and trustworthiness. The key takeaways of the MAPS dialogues are summarized in an article linked in the "resource" section below. 

A second edition of the MAPS Dialogues will be convened prior to the informal exchanges on AI in the military domain taking place in June 2026.

title: Geospatial AI (GeoAI) for Stabilization - Haiti

details.description:
Faster insights on costing and prioritizations can be achieved when geospatial technology is combined with artificial intelligence (GeoAI) to analyze large areas rapidly. This approach saves resources while still providing critical insights. UNDP fine-tuned a deep learning model to map damaged structures and obstacles using drone imagery. High-resolution drone imagery (5 cm) was acquired over the Port-au-Prince area in Haiti, covering a total area of 37.6 km² and including 170 neighborhoods at Administrative Level 4, either fully or partially. The main objective of this effort was to map damaged buildings, rubble piles, and barricades to support stabilization activities.

The core model used is based on the SAMLoRA architecture, originally deployed by Esri within ArcGIS Pro software. The SAMLoRA model combines the power of Segment Anything (SAM) with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), enabling precise object segmentation with minimal labeled data. It was fine-tuned to classify four classes: damaged buildings, debris, undamaged buildings, and background (such as streets and trees). The training dataset consisted of 1,427 image chips (320×320 pixels), with 80% allocated for training. The model achieved an overall accuracy of 81.7%, with F1-Scores of 75% for damaged buildings, 72% for debris, 87% for undamaged buildings, and 84.5% for background.

In addition to building damage detection, UNDP applied a GeoAI model to identify abandoned vehicles and areas of instability by detecting cars. This secondary model was based on the Mask R-CNN architecture, implemented using the ArcGIS API for Python, and was originally trained on various locations in the United States. Both models were deployed through the ArcGIS Enterprise Server (geosmart.undp.org).
details.technology_platform: ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS API for Python, ArcGIS Enterprise Server
details.ai_approach: deep learning model, GeoAI model based on Mask R-CNN

details.description: This research examined the opportunities and risks of AI from a WPS lens in Southeast Asia, with a focus on four types of gender biases in AI which will need to be addressed before the region can fully benefit from new technological developments; discrimination, stereotyping, exclusion, and insecurity. title: Can one-shot LLM feedback improve the quality of care delivered by frontline healthworkers in Nigeria?

details.description: This project tests whether a generalist LLM can improve the quality of care in community health clinics by providing “attending physician” style feedback to frontline health workers in Kano, Nigeria. In a blinded randomized evaluation, Medical Officers assess potential treatment errors in both original and LLM-assisted patient records created by Community Health Extension Workers (CHEWs). This test is intended to answer both whether the LLM is able to detect diagnostic or treatment mistakes in clinical practice, and whether CHEWs respond to such feedback by making better treatment decisions. To protect patients, actual diagnosis and treatment of the patient are decided by the Medical Officer before reviewing any information potentially affected by the LLM. The implementation – integration of one-shot LLM feedback into the English-language EMR of a small private clinic network- strips away technology and language-based frictions that would be encountered in typical clinical settings in Nigeria, in order to provide proof-of-concept evidence whether a (prompt-engineered) generalist LLM is capable of providing accurate and actionable feedback to frontline providers in low-resource settings that have the potential to improve patient care.

title: Pilot Damage Assessment and Early Recovery using GeoAI - Gaza

details.description:
Utilizing GeoAI models to detect damaged buildings and infrastructure and share the results with UNDP PAPP for response and planning actions. Geospatial artificial intelligence (GeoAI) is the application of artificial intelligence (AI) fused with geospatial data, science, and technology to accelerate real-world understanding of business opportunities, environmental impacts, and operational risks. Organizations are modernizing operations to run at scale through automated data generation and approachable spatial tools and algorithms. Extract rich geospatial data with deep learning. Save time by automating the extraction, classification, and detection of information from data such as imagery, video, point clouds, and text. Perform predictive analysis using machine learning. Build more accurate models. Detect clusters, calculate change, find patterns, and forecast outcomes with spatial algorithms backed by experts.

This project leverages GeoAI and high-resolution satellite imagery to support rapid damage assessment and early recovery planning in Gaza. By integrating artificial intelligence with geospatial data, UNDP aims to accelerate insights for effective crisis response and resource allocation.

A Maxar satellite image dated October 12, 2024 (50 cm resolution) covering the entire Gaza Strip served as the primary dataset. To create representative training samples, 13 sampling blocks were randomly selected, and 2,239 polygons representing destroyed and undestroyed areas were digitized. Additional background features such as roads and green spaces were treated as a third class. The image was divided into 256×256 pixel chips, generating 1,561 image tiles with corresponding masks for model training, with 20% reserved for validation.

The Esri-pretrained SAMLoRA model was selected for segmentation. SAMLoRA combines Segment Anything (SAM) with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), enabling precise object segmentation with minimal labeled data. The model classified three classes: destroyed, undestroyed, and background. Performance metrics demonstrated strong results: F1-score – 84% (undestroyed) and 87% (destroyed). The model was applied to classify new images dated January 25, July 8, and October 11, 2025, followed by post-processing and output cleaning.

The project was deployed on ArcGIS Enterprise Server (geosmart.undp.org) using ArcGIS Pro and ArcGIS API for Python and relied on ArcGIS deep learning frameworks for model training.

title: Baro Talent — Job Portal for the UN System

details.description:
Baro Talent is an experimental AI-driven job platform that automatically collects, analyzes, and categorizes job postings from 10 major UN organization pipelines (aggregating jobs from 30-40+ different agencies). Using advanced AI classification, the system automatically standardizes job titles, extracts key qualifications, identifies geographic postings, and applies intelligent keyword tagging—transforming scattered data into unified, searchable intelligence. This reduces the time professionals spend tracking opportunities from hours per week to minutes, while expanding access for early-career professionals and candidates from underrepresented regions who may lack networks to navigate the complex UN recruitment landscape.
By providing free, centralized access to UN career intelligence, Baro Talent supports workforce diversity and reduces barriers to entry for talent from the Global South, directly advancing equitable access to international development careers.

title: Crowdsourcing Safety: The Value of Passenger Feedback for Measuring Driving Safety

details.description: Crowdsourced data has shown promise to supplement traditional data sources for road safety, but the use of crowdsourced data in the public transport industry has been limited. Better understanding public transit driving behavior is particularly important in lower-income settings, where much of the population uses public buses yet buses comprise high crash rates. We examine the value added of crowdsourced data against telematics data using a case study of Kenya's public transit industry. Across a sample of minibuses, we enable passengers to provide feedback on buses by rating safety, speed, and by providing open ended comments; we also install telematics devices to capture objective measures of driving behavior. Overall, we find that crowdsourced passenger feedback provides accurate and actionable insight that both aligns with telematics data and goes beyond what is captured in telematics data. In particular, we leverage artificial intelligence to process open-ended comments; open-ended comments provide rich information about driving behavior, but unstructured text can be difficult to analyze. In particular, we demonstrate a straightforward approach of leveraging AI/LLMs to identify reports of safe and unsafe driving from comments; AI achieved higher accuracy compared to more traditional natural language processing approaches.
