title: World Trade Report 2025: Making trade and AI work together to the benefit of all

details.description: The 2025 edition of the World Trade Report explores how AI could shape inclusive, trade-led growth. It presents new findings that AI could substantially expand global trade between 34-37% across different scenarios and lift global GDP by over 12-13% by 2040 through lower trade costs and productivity gains. Trade, in turn, can make AI more accessible by helping economies access AI-enabling goods, such as raw materials, semiconductors and intermediate inputs. AI-enabled services show potential to create new trade opportunities. The report highlights that these benefits will depend on narrowing digital divides such as investing in education and training and deploying appropriate labour market policies; and having open and predictable trade policies. It examines the role of trade and trade-related policies in creating an enabling environment for more inclusive growth driven by AI. Finally, the report discusses the importance of international cooperation and in particular, the role of the WTO in fostering cooperation, addressing AI-related trade concerns, and promoting broader participation in agreements that can make AI technologies more accessible and affordable.

title: Human-Centered AI for Public Health: Co-Creating an HIV/STI Digital Platform with a local government

details.description:
This activity consisted of the collaborative design and development of a digital health platform for HIV and sexually transmitted infections (STIs) in the Municipality of Comodoro Rivadavia (Argentina). The initiative included a georeferenced platform of health services and an AI-enabled chatbot to provide confidential, accessible, and context-sensitive information to users.

The activity strengthened local government capacities in AI for public health through hands-on training, co-creation workshops, and interdisciplinary collaboration among municipal teams, health professionals, civil society organizations, and digital specialists. Participants learned how to map user needs, design responsible AI interactions, evaluate risks, and integrate AI tools into existing health workflows.
details.technology_platform:
Large Language Model API (OpenAI) for conversational responses.
Web development frameworks (React/Next.js) for building the public-facing platform.
Geospatial tools, an open-source GIS libraries, to power the georeferenced service map.
details.ai_approach:
Generative AI, enabling natural, context-sensitive responses to user queries.
Natural Language Processing (NLP) to interpret user intent and generate clear, accessible explanations about HIV and STI topics.
Large Language Models (LLMs) to power the chatbot’s conversational capabilities, ensuring high-quality, human-like interaction.
Human-in-the-loop alignment, ensuring that the AI complements (not replaces) health professionals and always invites users to seek human support when needed.
Responsible AI design, including guardrails, controlled domains of conversation, and content safety mechanisms to prevent misinformation.
User-centered AI interaction design, co-created with municipal health teams, civil society, and community stakeholders to ensure cultural, linguistic, and accessibility relevance.
details.testimonial:
As one participant put it: “I leave knowing that we are capable of creating a digital response by bringing together different disciplines and fields of knowledge”. Another added: “I learned that artificial intelligence is a tool that allows us to create, and that interdisciplinary collaboration is fundamental for designing human-centered solutions”.

What participants most valued was the collaborative and human atmosphere: “The empathy, the positive energy, and the clarity of concepts made all the difference”, one person shared. Another highlighted: “It was a dynamic and enjoyable workshop where everyone could express ideas freely”. Many discovered new technological tools, noting that “new possibilities opened up that we weren’t aware of”. Some were surprised to find other municipal departments working on similar issues: “I even learned about teams I didn’t know existed”. When we asked what could be improved, one answer stayed with us: “I was left wanting more”.

title: Agentic AI: a virtual assistant to help refugee entrepreneurs create their business plans in Paraguay

details.description:
Challenge: UNHCR focuses on livelihoods and economic inclusion as a pathway to protection, dignity, self-reliance, and support their integration into their host communities. UNHCR supports its partners and governments counterparts by:
- Providing seed capital for small businesses and orientation to access the labor market.
- Advocating with financial institutions for refugees to access banking services.
- Providing training programs and digital tools to help refugees develop viable business plans, particularly for those without digital skills

Solution: Co-designed with refugees, UNHCR Paraguay developed an AI-powered business planning assistant to help refugees and asylum-seekers transform ideas into sustainable businesses for applying to seed capital funding. The tool provides a guided journey from identifying customers and market strategy to calculating financial viability and creating an actionable roadmap. The tool incorporates Paraguay’s legal framework for business registration, guiding users through steps such as entity selection, tax ID requirements, and licensing. It offers a structured journey from market analysis to financial viability and an actionable roadmap.

Key Features:
-24/7 availability, breaking technical barriers and providing real-time projections.
-Legal compliance guidance tailored to Paraguayan regulations.
-Developed by MCO Argentina with support from the UNHCR Data Innovation Fund and regional experts.

Impact: Transforming refugee talent into economic development: strengthening dignity and autonomy. Provides personalized insights and future projections for strategic decisions for refugee entrepreneurs. Empowers refugees with dignity and autonomy, reducing aid dependency. Automated business plan evaluation and real-time reporting and reducing processing times for livelihood grants provided by UNHCR and partners.
details.testimonial: “Social entrepreneurship offers a powerful pathway to address critical unmet needs within our [refugee] communities. By fostering innovative solutions, we can build a more inclusive and equitable future for everyone.” - Venezuelan woman, focus group, Asunción

title: ZHAI - Zero Hunger AI

details.description: Compounding crises – including food insecurity, conflict, and diseases – threaten millions of lives worldwide. When emergencies occur, marginalized communities suffer the most, with limited ability to respond. Forecasting impending crises is crucial for anticipatory actions that build resilience against shocks, but existing predictive models are hindered by incomplete or outdated data sources and measures – especially since the halt of FEWS NET. ZHAI (ZeroHungerAI) utilizes novel natural language processing (NLP) methods on non-traditional data sources like news articles to uncover and track food insecurity risk factors. Our pilot improves food crises forecasts across 37 countries by up to 46%, predicting crises as far as a year in advance, even in data-scarce environments – enabling community organizations and local governments to take concrete, anticipatory actions that save citizens’ lives and decrease humanitarian costs. Beyond predictions, our approach offers continuous, near-real-time insights into the drivers of crises outbreaks – offering stakeholders, such as local governments, crucial information which empowers them to tailor the response to crises’ unique local conditions. Supported by Google.org, we are turning the research pilot into a live public good, with weekly, district-level updates on food insecurity risks across all 78 International Development Association (IDA) countries.
details.ai_approach: novel natural language processing (NLP) methods, predictive models

title: Vendor Risk Analysis

details.description:
The Vendor Risk Analysis (VRA) Workflow is an AI-assisted system designed to produce accurate, audit-ready vendor risk reports through a structured, multi-stage process. It combines AI-driven report generation with two complementary verification methods to ensure reliability and compliance:

Link Analysis validates that every URL cited in the report is accessible and accurately supports the referenced statement, ensuring citation integrity and source trustworthiness.

Claim Analysis independently fact-checks each claim in the report, whether or not it has a cited link, by segmenting content into semantically complete units and verifying them against external sources, ensuring factual correctness.
details.technology_platform:
Frontend: Microsoft Teams integration for Prompt Manager;  Streamlit and Gradiofor workflow execution.
Backend: Python-based orchestration for report generation, segmentation, and verification.
Core AI Components: Generative AI Models (OpenAI GPT family, Azure AI):
Used for initial report drafting and linguistic segmentation of claims.
Rule-Based & NLP Techniques: Identify factual claims and semantically complete units.
Web Search Integration: For independent claim verification during Claim Analysis.
details.ai_approach:
Stage 1: Vendor Risk Assessment
Gather inputs: product name, intended use, and VRA prompt template.
Access UNU Prompt Manager via Teams for standardized prompts.

Stage 2: Report Generation
Generate initial VRA report using AI-assisted drafting.
Apply segmentation to break content into analysis units (semantically complete sentences or phrases).

Stage 3: Link Analysis
Validate that each URL cited in the report supports the corresponding unit.
Confirm link validity and content accuracy (critical for audits and controversial claims).

Stage 4: Claim Analysis
Independently fact-check claims using external sources without relying on provided URLs.
Apply linguistic and AI-based verification for accuracy and completeness.


Workflow Benefits
Accuracy: Dual verification reduces misinformation risk.
Compliance: Supports audit-ready standards.
Efficiency: AI-driven segmentation and prompt management accelerate report preparation.

title: Exploring the Landscape of Data Use in the Development Economics Literature using Large Language Models (AI and LLMs)

details.description: This project aims to build a Database of Data Use by developing AI models to detect when and how data is mentioned or used in documents. Just as citation databases like Google Scholar have transformed our ability to measure the impact of research, this initiative aims to create a framework for assessing the utility and impact of data. By systematically tracking data use, we can better understand the return on investment in data production, identify data gaps, and guide future funding and policy decisions. However, this challenge cannot be solved through manual methods. There is no widely adopted standard for citing data; references often appear in inconsistent or unstructured forms. AI makes this task feasible for the first time. By learning to recognize the context in which data is referenced, regardless of how it is cited or described, AI enables scalable and intelligent detection of data use across large volumes of text. By uncovering where and how data is used—or not—this project helps ensure that development efforts are grounded in evidence and that investments in data yield real-world impact.

title: Being a Public Servant in Namibia - The Pocket Guide

details.description:
“Being a Public Servant in Namibia: The Pocket Guide” is a co-created suite of learning and governance tools developed by UNDP Namibia's Accelerator Lab, in partnership with the Government of Namibia. Designed for the country’s largest workforce, approximately 125,000 public servants in a nation of 3 million people, the Pocket Guide modernises public service orientation, induction, strengthens ethical conduct, and improves access to staff rules and regulations.

The suite consists of three integrated elements:

1. The Pocket Guide & Handbook: Available in digital and printed formats for all public servants.

2. Nine Micro-Learning Modules:  An onboarding curriculum introducing public servants to ethics, conduct, rules, the Public Service Charter, governance values, and everyday professionalism.

3. The Pocket Bot:  A conversational AI trained on Namibia’s public service acts, regulations, staff rules, and administrative procedures, providing instant, accurate answers.

The Pocket Guide suite has strengthened Namibia’s public sector learning ecosystem by:
Making public service rules, regulations, and ethical standards accessible, understandable, and actionable.
Providing the first AI-powered Pocket Bot dedicated to Namibia’s public service, reducing information bottlenecks and enabling faster decision-making.
Enhancing induction across ministries through micro-learning modules that are short, practical, and accessible on any device.
Promoting culture change through co-creation, shared responsibility, and peer-led ethics conversations.
Improving the quality of service delivery by ensuring public servants have reliable, instant access to the principles that govern their work.

The solutions were co-created with the help of UNDP Namibia's IT Analyst, Dr Maria Ausiku, together  the public service, bringing together more than 150 ethics and integrity champions, HR practitioners, and multidisciplinary teams from central government, regional councils, and local authorities. The process amplified collective intelligence and built ownership across the ecosystem.
